sections.title: Framing then versus now
sections.content: Reflecting on how something has changed needs a clear before/after frame. azelőtt ("before that, back then") sets the earlier state, azóta ("since then") sets everything that has happened up to now, and megváltozik ("to change") — an -ik verb, past tense (meg)változtam, (meg)változtál, (meg)változott — names the change itself.

items.spanish: Azelőtt féltem az új helyzetektől, azóta sokat változtam.
items.english: Before, I was afraid of new situations; since then, I've changed a lot.

items.spanish: Sokat megváltozott a városunk az elmúlt tíz évben.
items.english: Our city has changed a lot over the last ten years.

sections.content: azelőtt and korábban (from Unit 1) overlap but aren't identical: korábban just means "earlier" in a story, while azelőtt specifically points back to before the change or moment you're currently discussing — pair it naturally with azóta on the other side of that same dividing line.
